The fallback of the nearest [``](https://react.dev/reference/react/Suspense) boundary takes its place in the shell, and the deferred content renders once one of those happens. It is meant to defer content that the App Shell would otherwise render, typically content that depends on session data and is expensive to generate. During a build-time prerender nothing is deferred, so content below `prefetch()` is prerendered as usual. ## Usage The function requires [Cache Components](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/cacheComponents) and throws an error if not enabled. Without [Partial Prefetching](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/partialPrefetching) a route has no App Shell, so the function has no effect. Enable Partial Prefetching globally, or one route at a time, by [adopting Partial Prefetching](/docs/app/guides/adopting-partial-prefetching). ```ts filename="next.config.ts" highlight={4,5} import type { NextConfig } from 'next' const nextConfig: NextConfig = { cacheComponents: true, partialPrefetching: true, } export default nextConfig ``` A route is then rendered in three stages, and content can arrive at any of them: 1. The App Shell, which every `` into the route prefetches, and which holds the part of the route that does not depend on the URL. 2. A per-link prefetch, requested with [``](/docs/app/api-reference/components/link#prefetch), which resolves the URL and adds the content that depends on it. 3. The navigation itself, which covers everything left. Awaiting `prefetch()` keeps content out of the App Shell, so it renders only on a per-link prefetch or on the navigation. To keep content out of per-link prefetches as well, so it renders only on the navigation, use [`navigation()`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/navigation). Everything above `prefetch()` renders in the App Shell, and everything below renders on a per-link prefetch or on the navigation. Deferral is scoped to the component that awaits it and the tree below: sibling branches render in the shell as usual. Place it above the work to defer, and wrap the component in [``](https://react.dev/reference/react/Suspense): ```tsx filename="app/dashboard/page.tsx" highlight={25} switcher import { Suspense } from 'react' import { cookies } from 'next/headers' import { cacheLife, prefetch } from 'next/cache' export default function Page() { return ( <> Loading greeting...

}> {/* in the App Shell */} Loading recommendations...

}> {/* the fallback is in the App Shell, the recommendations are not */} ) } async function Greeting() { const session = (await cookies()).get('session')?.value return

{session ? 'Welcome back' : 'Welcome'}

} async function Recommendations()

events.content:
The dashboard now prefetches only each project's title. The rest of the project page loads after you click.

I ran `npx next build` and it passed (exit 0). `/projects/[slug]` builds as a partial prerender. With `npx next start`, a full load of `/projects/acme` renders the title, description and activity. I didn't check the prefetch requests in a browser, so I haven't directly confirmed that the title is instant and the details aren't prefetched. That behaviour comes from the Next 16.4 canary docs.

Changes:
- **`next.config.ts`**: turned on `partialPrefetching: true`. A plain link only prefetches the parts of a page that don't depend on the URL. The title depends on the project slug, so it needs the next change.
- **`app/page.tsx`**: the dashboard links now use `prefetch={true}`, which asks the server for this project's own data ahead of the click. That's what lets the title appear instantly.
- **`app/projects/[slug]/page.tsx`**: split the page into two separately loading parts:
  - `ProjectTitle` loads the slug and `getProjectTitle`, and is included in the prefetch.
  - `ProjectDetails` calls `await navigation()` before `getProjectDetails`. Everything after that call is left out of all prefetches, so the slow details request (800 ms) only runs when you actually navigate. Until then, "Loading details..." shows. It's still cached with `use cache`.

Before, the page loaded the title and details together, so the title had to wait for the details.

The build also changed `tsconfig.json` on its own: it set `jsx` to `react-jsx`, added `.next/dev/types/**/*.ts` to `include`, and reformatted the arrays. Next makes these changes on every build or dev run. I left them in place, and you can revert them if you don't want them.
